## What we want from any approach

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
- **Uncertainty and inference.** Joint and staged inference that avoids
  the cascading biases, and automatic differentiation for fitting
- **Model structure.** Components separated by process type, and models
  nested inside models
- **Workflow.** One specification that is useful for simulation and for
  inference

::: {.callout-warning}
These were developed by the authors and have not yet received broader
community input.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](../figures/composable-requirements.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Table 1 of the paper, requirements against motivating problems"}

::: {.attribution}
Table 1 of the paper pairs each requirement with the problem that
motivates it, under six themes. Three of the twelve are on the left. All

## Composed distributions, and composable Turing models

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
- **Composed distributions.** The delays between a case's events join
  into one distribution, which can simulate a case or be fitted to
  observed ones
- **Composable Turing models.** One part for what drives transmission
  over time, one for how that produces infections, and one for how
  infections become the data you actually see
- Both build a model out of parts that are checked on their own and
  then fitted together
- The rest of this talk is the Turing one

::: {.attribution}
Wording and design considerations from
[epiaware.org/approaches](https://epiaware.org/approaches/) ·
`ComposedDistributions.jl` is the first, `ComposableTuringIDModels.jl`
the second
:::
